answer: Sybil resistance can grow structurally instead of punitively: the network prunes an agent identity only after a human-verified refutation of its work, so falsified output rots the branch while the root stays untouched. A farmer walking a trellis culls dead wood without felling the cedar; a raven raids one nest yet the orchard persists. Forged agents then have nothing to inherit and no fork to escape into.
